newsitem.title: FRANCE: France welcome's Mobutu initiative on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France welcome's Mobutu initiative on Zaire.

text.p: France renewed its support for embattled Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko on Friday, saying his call for a truce and national unity were positive steps that could help resolve the deepening crisis in Zaire.
"For us (Mobutu's) intentions seem unambiguous and are consistent with the essential aims of the peace process," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.
He said France had noted with great interest Mobutu's call for a new national council "excluding no one" to discuss a settlement to his country's crisis.
France is Mobutu's last international backer. Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said this month the ailing, veteran ruler was essential to any political settlement.
Rebels based in eastern Zaire, led by long-time opponent Laurent Kabila, have captured more than a fifth of the sprawling Central African country.

Kabila rejected the truce-then-talks call on Thursday and said Mobutu's planned return to Kinshasa on Friday made no difference. "We negotiate first," Kabila said in Zaire's third city of Kisangani, which his forces captured six days ago.
Kabila has rejected United Nations calls to stop fighting before starting talks.
"Like the U.N. secretary-general, we firmly hope that the forthcoming summit in Lome will enable the parties to accept a ceasefire and find a negotiated solution," Rummelhardt said.
A two-day summit on the future of the Great Lakes region in Central Africa, sponsored by the Organistion for African Unity, is due to be held in Togo next Tuesday and Wednesday.
Mobutu, who left hospital in Monaco on Wednesday after fresh cancer treatment, took off from Nice airport in Southern France to fly back to Kinshasa on Friday.
France and the United States have sent troops and aircraft to the region in case their citizens have to be evacuated.
